name: Missouri Fox Trotter
notes: The saddle horse of the Ozark country of southern Missouri and northern Arkansas, organised at Ava in 1948 and the Missouri state horse since 2002. The fox trot is a broken four-beat diagonal - the front foot of a pair lands just before the opposite hind, one foot is always down, and the horse covers about ten miles an hour doing it all day.
Gaited near-fixed on DMRT3, alongside the flat-footed walk and canter the registry also requires.

The registry is colour-open and the pool is the widest natural palette that ships outside the Mustang: bay, brown, black, chestnut, palomino, buckskin, cremello, dun, grey, roan, champagne, tobiano, sabino and frame all belong. The rulebook has its own champagne classes - classic, amber, gold and ivory - which is the rare case of a registry naming the locus for us.
Frame is here at a real rate, so this is one of the breeds where two founders can produce a lethal white foal. That is the breed being what it is, not an oversight.
The leopard complex is forced wild: it is explicitly outside the documented range. Pearl, mushroom, dominant white and brindle have no support either.

Silver is at a modest rate and carries a caveat the draft raised and then got right: MCOA in this breed is a consequence of the silver PMEL variant, not a separate disorder locus, and PPIB is HERDA and belongs to Quarter Horse cutting lines. Neither was seeded as a disease.
All disorders clear. UC Davis offers a PSSM1 test in a Fox Trotter context, but the existence of a test is not a founder rate, so nothing was assigned.
Curly-coated Fox Trotters occur and there is no curly locus in the mod to give them. Curl is not required for breed identity here anyway.
The separate 11-to-14-hand pony registry is not modelled; the band is the documented 14-16-hand saddle horse.
The fox trot itself, the head nod, the sliding hind action and rider comfort are none of them modelled.
